clue.text: Ensured article attached to peg is collected by sentry

indicators.note: a thing collected by someone is taken in and held, so the sentry word encloses the rest

parts.note: a sentry is a guard on watch
an is the indefinite article
a tee is the little peg a golf ball sits on

explanation.surface: Someone makes sure of something by hanging an item on a hook for a guard to pick up.
explanation.walkthrough: Peg is the golfer's tee; the sentry is a guard, opened up to take the article and peg.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made certain of an outcome is to have assured it, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: State university starts to treat academics humanely

indicators.note: the starts of the following three words are their opening letters, one from each

explanation.surface: A state university is urged to deal kindly with its lecturers.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty US states, so the definition gives an example category.

clue.text: Speed of old car — not the maximum speed

indicators.note: not here tells us to drop the letter for the top speed from the old-car word

parts.note: a crate is slang for a battered old car
c is the physicist's symbol for the speed of light, the fastest anything can go

explanation.surface: An old banger is said to be slow, never reaching its top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: c, the speed of light, is the universe's speed limit; take it out of CRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rate is a pace or velocity, so a synonym for speed.

clue.text: Country road that man's overturned on

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on another sits above it
in a down clue something overturned is turned upside down, so the man's name reads upwards

parts.note: Ron is a man's name, standing for 'that man'
a way is a road or path

explanation.surface: A country lane on which some fellow has flipped his vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns RON into NOR, and 'on' sets it above WAY in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a Scandinavian nation, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Latin — it's sexiest possibly for certain philosophers

indicators.note: possibly says the letters given could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that Latin is the most alluring language, as some thinkers might argue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the fifteen letters of LATIN, ITS and SEXIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartre and Camus belonged to the school of thought stressing individual existence and free choice.

clue.text: Old scoundrel heading north with Italian robber

indicators.note: in a down entry heading north means reading upwards, so the old scoundrel's letters run backwards

parts.note: a cad is an ungentlemanly rogue
IT is an abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A villain of the past travels north with an Italian thief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' reverses OCAD to DACO in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacoit is a member of an armed gang of bandits in India or Burma.

clue.text: Spoils seeds getting spilt outside box

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled seeds letters sit around the box word
seeds that are spilt scatter, so their letters come out jumbled

parts.note: a crate is a box for transporting goods

explanation.surface: Seeds tipped out of a box go to waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting spilt' scrambles SEEDS into DESES, which 'outside' wraps round the box word. Spoils is a verb, not loot.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil a holy place is to defile or profane it, a verb in the same tense.

clue.text: Man is one such — is allowed to waste time

indicators.note: to waste a thing is to lose it, so the time letter is removed from the allowed word

parts.note: let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Someone has permission to dawdle.
explanation.walkthrough: Man here is the Isle of Man, the island between Britain and Ireland, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so the definition names an example.

clue.text: One's obviously been fired in a situation involving criminality

definitions.text: One's obviously been fired in a situation involving criminality

parts.words: One's obviously been fired in a situation involving criminality
parts.note: a firearm still giving off fumes has clearly just been discharged, and the phrase also means conclusive proof of a crime

explanation.surface: Someone has been dismissed from a job after shady dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests sacking; it is a weapon discharged.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means undeniable evidence of wrongdoing, from a weapon still warm after use.

clue.text: Convert quiet from what we hear — one may be seen in church

definitions.text: one may be seen in church

indicators.note: what we hear signals the words are taken by their sound, not spelling

parts.note: to convert something is to alter it; quiet as a noun means peace, calm

explanation.surface: A preacher hopes to win souls by quietness, judging from reports.
explanation.walkthrough: Convert is a verb here, not a religious convert, despite the church setting.
explanation.definitionFit: An altarpiece is a painted or carved work behind the altar, typically found in a place of worship.

clue.text: Drill bringing fatigue

explanation.surface: A dull exercise that wears people out.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore is a hole made with a drill or the act of drilling one; to bore also means to tire with dullness.

clue.text: Hindrance restricting soldiers one politician gets to change

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the change word surrounds the soldiers word

parts.note: to edit is to revise or change text
men is a common term for soldiers or troops

explanation.surface: An obstacle that holds back troops, as a lone politician seeks reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' puts the soldiers inside the change word; one and the politician come first. Change looks like a noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An impediment is an obstruction, a synonym that also covers a speech defect.

clue.text: Pigeon enthusiast followed by dog

parts.note: a fan is a keen follower
to dog someone is to tail them, follow closely

explanation.surface: A bird-lover trailed by a hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' looks like the animal but is a verb meaning follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The fantail is a domestic breed of pigeon with a spread, fan-shaped tail.

clue.text: Relish patronage, pocketing pounds

indicators.note: pocketing means taking inside, so the patronage word swallows the pounds letter

parts.note: favour is support or patronage given by a superior
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a patron's support while lining their pockets with cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketing' puts L inside FAVOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish as a noun means taste or savour, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Neil perhaps in formation on sports field

parts.note: the answer read as instructions says to rearrange a four-letter word, and the name Neil is one such rearrangement

explanation.surface: A player called Neil may take his place in the team's shape on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer split in two is an anagram instruction whose result is the clue's Neil. Rugby players line up in two rows for a throw-in.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union, players form parallel lines to contest a throw from touch, a set formation.

clue.text: Little boy blessing everyone, see, at the right moment

parts.note: Tiny Tim, the sickly boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol, says God bless us, every one
Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A child gives a benediction to all at just the right time.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is the area a bishop governs; Ely is a favourite crossword see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well-timed or opportune happens when it should, a synonym.

clue.text: Rioter with gun's out stealing

indicators.note: out signals letters thrown out of order

parts.note: the possessive s is kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: A rioter pulls a gun and goes looting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges RIOTER and GUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousering is slang for pocketing money dishonestly, a synonym for taking.

clue.text: Row about one daughter — should be smarter

indicators.note: about means going round, so the row word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
I is the Roman numeral one
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A family quarrel over a daughter who ought to dress more neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I and D inside TIER after its T. Row looks like a quarrel but is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Neater and more presentable is a comparative synonym, matching in degree.

clue.text: Boss of boat race crew possibly drunk?

definitions.text: Boss of boat race crew possibly

explanation.surface: The cox of a rowing eight may have had a few too many.
explanation.walkthrough: The cox directing a rowing eight sits facing and above them; the phrase also means tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The cox controls the eight-oar boat from the stern; the idiom means slightly intoxicated.

clue.text: Mistake having one fielder close to the wicket?

definitions.text: having one fielder close to the wicket

explanation.surface: A captain errs by posting a catcher near the batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a slip is a close catching fielder beside the wicketkeeper; slip up means a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder or error; and in cricket a slip fielder moved in close to the batsman.

clue.text: Something likely to explode? Depart in a frenzy

indicators.note: a frenzy is wild disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Leave in a panic before a bomb goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a frenzy' rearranges DEPART.
explanation.definitionFit: A petard is a small bomb for blasting doors, as in hoist with one's own.

clue.text: Heralds put almost a whole month around castle

indicators.note: around says the trimmed month surrounds the castle letter
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: August is a month of the year
the castle in chess is the rook, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: Messengers spend almost the whole summer month near a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims AUGUST to AUGUS, and 'around' puts R inside it. Castle is the chess rook.
explanation.definitionFit: To augur is to foreshadow or presage, a verb matching the definition in form.

clue.text: Attack made by fool on excellent learner

parts.note: an ass is a fool
A1 means first-rate, written with I for the one
L is for learner, from the L-plates on British cars driven by learners

explanation.surface: An idiot sets upon a brilliant student.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, first-class, is written AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to assault or set upon, a verb synonym.

clue.text: One has no fancy ideas about joining the top celebs

parts.note: re means concerning or about
the A-list is the most famous tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth person among famous people.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatist who sees things as they are is a person without illusions.

clue.text: Bank in free fall

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words free fall, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A riverbank collapsing without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free fall' looks like the subject; the answer is tucked across those two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge or bank of rock or sand near the water's surface.

clue.text: It's a game, getting the tail off a fish

indicators.note: losing its tail means the last letter of the fish word is dropped

parts.note: a skate is a flat ray-like fish

explanation.surface: Removing a fish's tail is a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the tail off' removes E from SKATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Skat is a three-player German card game.

clue.text: Reject nothing after check to assess suitability

indicators.note: after says the nothing letter comes behind the check word

parts.note: to vet is to examine someone carefully before approval
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Turn something down without inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a refusal or block, and to veto is to turn down, a verb match.

clue.text: Chain put on male animal falling apart

indicators.note: in an across entry a piece put on another follows it

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a shackle is a chain or fetter

explanation.surface: A tether is fitted to a ram that is collapsing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilapidated building is tumbledown, nearly in ruins, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Absence of drink not given a mention

parts.note: no expresses absence, as in no entry

indicators.note: not given means the letter A is withheld from the phrase

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A lack of refreshment goes unremarked.
explanation.walkthrough: Absence of drink is NO TEA; take away A.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to remark on it, a verb synonym; a note is also a brief mention.

clue.text: Terribly isolated, getting on — a recipe for misery

indicators.note: terribly here signals the letters are badly disordered

explanation.surface: Being cut off from others while ageing leads to unhappiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges ISOLATED and ON; 'getting on' looks like ageing but simply supplies ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak wretchedness and grief are a synonym of misery.
